name: Cubase Pro
tagline: Full fat DAW for recording, MIDI sequencing, editing and mixing music.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Cubase is roughly forty years of DSP, a real time audio engine, a plugin host, a MIDI sequencer, a score editor, an audio warping engine and a mixer that does not glitch at 64 samples of latency. An agent can give you a browser multitrack recorder in an afternoon, and that is genuinely useful for voice memos and rough demos, but it is not the same category of object. The hard parts are the parts nobody demos: driver level latency, sample accurate automation, plugin delay compensation, crash safe recording of a take you cannot ask the drummer to play again. On top of that, your existing projects, templates, key commands and VST collection all live inside its format. The only honest DIY answer is a small recorder that does one tenth of one percent of the job, pleasantly.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app that records and arranges multiple audio tracks on a timeline with per track volume, mute and solo, then bounces the mix to a WAV file.
requirements: Node 20 and a modern Chromium browser
An audio interface or at least a decent USB mic
Local disk space for raw takes
Patience with browser audio input latency
whatYouLose: VST and VST3 plugin hosting, which is most of why anyone buys a DAW
ASIO class low latency monitoring while tracking
MIDI sequencing, virtual instruments, the key editor and the score editor
Audio warping, comping across lanes, pitch correction and real automation
Crash recovery, project versioning and the ability to open your old sessions
moatNotes: The plugin ecosystem is the real lock: your reverbs, your instruments, your templates all assume a host that behaves like Cubase.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a DAW is measured in milliseconds and in the absence of surprises. People pay for an engine that keeps timing under load, compensates plugin latency without being asked, survives a crash mid take, and opens a project from 2014 with all its automation intact. They also pay because the whole third party instrument and effect industry targets VST, and because their fingers already know the key commands. None of that is reproducible in a session, or a month, by anyone.
notes: A browser multitrack recorder is a weekend build; a sample accurate plugin host with sub 10ms round trip latency is not. The moat is decades of real time audio engineering plus an entire VST industry built on top of it.
prompt:
Build a local, offline multitrack audio recorder called "Tapehead". No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + TypeScript + React, Web Audio API and MediaRecorder for capture, IndexedDB for storage, plain CSS. No backend. No audio libraries beyond what the browser ships.

In scope:
- Project list in IndexedDB: create, rename, delete a project.
- Inside a project, add audio tracks. Each track has a name, volume, pan, mute and solo.
- Record from a selected input device via getUserMedia into a track, with device picker and an input level meter.
- Recording a take while other tracks play back, aligned to the transport start position.
- A timeline view: clips drawn as waveform blocks, draggable in time, trimmable at both edges.
- Transport: play, stop, record, loop region, playhead scrubbing, a bar showing seconds.
- Mixdown: render all tracks through GainNode and StereoPannerNode via OfflineAudioContext and export a 44.1kHz stereo WAV. Write the WAV encoder by hand.
- Import existing WAV or MP3 files onto a track by drag and drop.
- Store raw recordings as Blobs in IndexedDB; never lose a take on reload.

Out of scope, do not attempt: VST or any plugin hosting, MIDI, virtual instruments, time stretching, pitch correction, comping lanes, automation curves, sub 10ms monitoring. Say so in the README.

Details:
- Monitor input is off by default, with a checkbox and a clear warning about feedback and latency.
- Keyboard: space to play/stop, R to arm record, S to solo focused track, M to mute.
- Autosave project state on every change, debounced.
- Include a README stating the known latency limits of browser audio and that this is a sketchpad, not a DAW.
- No .env needed since there are no secrets. If you add one, explain why.
